messages:
incidents-bot: [ALERT] Severity: P1 — gpu-pool-saturation detected in eu1. Queue length for primary-gpu-pool > 15k, 99p token latency 12s, 429 spikes for top customers. Autoscale attempted 3 times, failures with "quotaExceeded". Runbook: https://docs.redwood.ai/runbooks/gpu-pool-saturation 

maya (oncall): on it. paging eng-sre and routing. starting quick triage. can someone confirm if autoscaler hit gcp quota or internal cap? :pager:

liam (routing): looking now. routing logs show spillover attempts to eu2 but weight is low (0.1). policy = prefer-local. I see consistent 502/503 from proxy when backend pool is overloaded.

arya (runtime): autoscaler logs show requests to cloud provider returned HTTP 429 quota. also see node provisioning stuck at "Creating" for 14m. cloud account shows GPU quota 0 available in eu1 zone.

maya (oncall): ok -- impact: customers on eu1 experiencing delayed generations and some 429s. High-throughput tenants (chatburst) seeing errors. tagging @customer-facing to notify top customers.

customer-facing (jess): notified top 5 customers via status page and email. noting severity and ongoing mitigation. will update in 15m.

liam (routing): mitigation proposal: increase spillover to eu2 to 40% for affected models and enable immediate fallback routing for requests > 3s queue wait. can do manual override via console or `rwctl` CLI. which is preferred?

maya (oncall): do it. we want fastest path — CLI override and update routing-svcs policy. liaise with runtime to ensure eu2 has capacity and model variants match.

liam (routing): executing now: 

```
# temporary: shift 40% of traffic for model family 'redwood-base' to eu2
rwctl route override --model redwood-base --region eu2 --weight 0.4 --reason "eu1 gpu saturation"
```
...response: 200 OK. routing-svcs reports new weights propagated to edge in ~22s.

routing-svcs: propagation complete. health-checks show eu2 accepting connections. small spike in latency for some requests as caches warm.

arya (runtime): confirming eu2 pool has capacity for the extra traffic. autoscaler there is healthy. starting cache prewarm for top models. KV cache miss rate will be high for first 3–5 minutes.

maya (oncall): monitoring metrics... queue length in eu1 dropping from 15k -> 9k in last 6m, 99p latency dropping to 7s. 429 rate falling but still elevated for a subset of customers.

sre-lead (noah): quick note — why didn't autoscaler fall back to burst capacity? check config for reservedBurst=false. we may need to check Dedicated pool limits vs host quotas. If quota is global per project, cross-region won't help provisioning.

arya (runtime): checked. reservedBurst was disabled in eu1 due to cost constraints; autoscaler respects project-level GPU quota so provisioning failed. we will open quota request but that's not quick. For immediate relief, routing spillover is the fastest. Also there's an internal limit that prevents scaling above 120 cards in eu1; that cap hit last night during maintenance.

liam (routing): FYI — increased spillover to 60% for high-QPS routes that are tolerant to cross-region latency. Using `rwctl` again for selective model routes. This should reduce failure rates for bursty tenants.

maya (oncall): handoff: I'm going to hand routing/drain to liam and runtime tuning to arya. I'll stay on the thread for customer updates but switching primary responder to liam.

liam (routing): taking over. immediate checklist: 1) monitor eu2 error rates and token-cost impact, 2) ensure sticky sessions for stateful workloads aren't broken, 3) watch for rate limits in eu2. Also starting canary rollback plan in case eu2 shows issues.

ops-runner-bot: runbook step executed: manual route override applied and cached. Note: set flag `spillover-override=true` in control plane for audit.

customer-facing (jess): ETA note for customers: mitigation in progress, partial reroute to eu2 applied. Some customers will see slightly higher latency but fewer errors. Will post a status update now.

maya (oncall): logs: grep of proxy errors shows backend `primary-gpu-pool` returning `HTTP 503: overloaded` and `x-retry-after` absent. We should enable client-side retry headers temporarily. Can runtime add `Retry-After` 5s on overload?

arya (runtime): yes, enabling graceful throttling header on edge for 503s. Pushing config now: 

```
edge-config set --throttle-header "Retry-After: 5"
```
applied. Also enabling queuing prioritization for small requests to reduce tail latencies.

liam (routing): seeing outbound egress to eu2 increase ~3x. No immediate quota alarms yet, but I'll set alerts on eu2 95p cpu/gpu utilization.

maya (oncall): customer impact assessment: ~12 customers with heavy bursts saw >30% error increase before mitigation; majority now within acceptable error budgets. open incident SOC ticket for billing team re: cost delta.

sre-lead (noah): documented immediate mitigations: (a) routing spillover increase, (b) edge retry headers, (c) cache prewarm in eu2, (d) manual burst capacity review. Next steps: quota request escalation and postmortem to look at reserve policies.

liam (routing): status update: eu1 queue ~6.2k, eu2 traffic ~+42%, overall 429 rate back down to baseline for tier-1 customers, some tier-2 still seeing intermittent 5xx.

maya (oncall): adding timeline note for handoff: "Root cause: GPU quota exhaustion + hard cap on pool size in eu1 during peak burst. Mitigation: temporary routing override to eu2 + edge throttling. Handoff to liam for routing & arya for runtime until stabilization."

liam (routing): I'll continue monitoring for the next 45m and then start a gradual rollback of spillover once eu1 queue < 2k and 99p latency < 1.5s for 10m window.

customer-facing (jess): posted status: "Partial mitigation: traffic rerouted to eu2; errors reduced. Engineers actively monitoring; follow-up scheduled." Link: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2173334444

maya (oncall): handover complete. liam/arya you're primary. I'll remain available for customer comms. tagging @sre-lead for postmortem.

liam (routing): acknowledged. will post stabilizing notes and create a runbook addendum for cross-region spillover thresholds and reservedBurst recommendations.

arya (runtime): creating alert to flag project GPU quota at 20% remaining and better telemetry for autoscaler failure reasons (quota vs internal cap).

sre-lead (noah): thanks team. good mitigation. we'll schedule a retro and action items: quota requests, reservedBurst revisit, and update the routing policy default to be less prefer-local for high-burst workloads.

maya (oncall): closing paging loop for now — incident remains active but stabilized. will update thread with final impact numbers and postmortem link. :white_check_mark:
